keyVerseText: And Adam said, This is now bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh: she shall be called Woman, because she was taken out of Man. Woman: Heb. Isha Man: Heb. Ish
rootMeaning: The root of עֶצֶם (ʻetsem) comes from the verb עָצַם (ʻâtsam), which conveys ideas of strength, closure, and increase in power or size. This root sense of being strong, mighty, or closely bound enriches the noun beyond the simple English gloss of 'bone' or 'body,' highlighting not only the physical structure but also the inherent strength and essence that bones represent. Thus, ʻetsem carries a depth that includes both the literal framework of the body and the figurative substance or self.
usageInScripture: Throughout Scripture, עֶצֶם is predominantly translated as 'bone' or 'bones,' appearing 126 times and often referring to the physical bones of a person or animal. The top translations such as 'and the bones,' 'my bones,' and 'the bones' reveal a consistent emphasis on the tangible, structural aspect of the body. However, the word also extends figuratively to mean 'life,' 'strength,' or 'selfsame,' showing its flexibility in conveying both concrete and abstract ideas of essence and vitality.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding עֶצֶם as both bone and essence deepens our appreciation for the biblical portrayal of human identity as created and sustained by God. Bones signify strength and the very framework of life, pointing to the intimate craftsmanship of God in forming man. The word’s layered meaning reminds believers that our physical bodies are not mere shells but integral to our being, reflecting God’s power and purpose. This connection between body and essence underscores the Christian hope in resurrection and the redemption of the whole person—body and soul—through Christ.
keyVerseReflection: In Genesis 2:23, Adam declares, 'This is now bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh,' using עֶצֶם to express a profound unity and shared essence between man and woman. The word ʻetsem here emphasizes not only the physical connection but also the deep, intrinsic bond that defines human relationships as God intended. This verse highlights the foundational truth that woman was taken from man’s very structure, affirming the dignity and equality of both as part of God’s creation.
